merged.angle: (A) resize: score each agent on its last year of track record (recordWindow = 252 ticks, not the 90-tick trailing window) and rank by shrunk Sharpe itself rather than Sharpe ÷ vol (the Kelly weight)

(C) carry-over: loop 1's close() proposal (c3-0.diff) ported onto the current HEAD d2151ed, which has the volatility-scaled ladder. Kept: a stop-out is one DelegationTree.close(agent) that takes back the agent's capital and every sub-budget it delegated. Also kept: AgentSpec.subMandates reserved at grant, the per-tick tree audit, and delegate() refusing under a revoked ancestor. Added hardening: shares are validated and cut in integer ppm; grows are clipped to the parent's available authority, so the book never makes a move the tree refuses; the audit runs twice per tick, before the tick trades (after onTick) and at its end; the stopped/live checks follow revocation up the chain; the core audit test now covers purposes. Cut rung re-decided on the check block: it stays on by default, and the type now allows leaving it unset.

loops.title: An operator is one counterparty (G), and every order is sized from the tree (R)
loops.note: Both structural: no utility claimed. On block B the center book returns 14.41% vs 8.63% for guardrails, with max drawdown 6.63% vs 6.53% (5.88% at the guardrails' volatility). A drawdown-cutting crowd limit won block A but failed block B in combination.

merged.angle: (G) STRUCTURE retry of loop 2's operator credit event. When one of an operator's names is stopped out, its other live names are capped as a group, in one applyTargets plan, at cutFactor x their FULL SIZE: the capital the allocator currently gives them uncut. That is share x deployable at the latest reallocation, or the equal initial allocation before warmup. The cut is a ceiling on capital (cutToCeiling: min(capital, cf x fullSize)), not a multiplier on what the name holds, and the ladder cut and the operator cap are one ceiling. So they never compound: (1) a name the ladder cut, or cut and restored but still at half capital, is not halved again; (2) a name an earlier operator event capped is not cut again; (3) a reallocation takes min(ladderMult, capMult), not the product; (4) the ladder's own cut of an already-capped name is a no-op. Each name keeps its own ladder, and nothing in the operator code writes a ladder state or revokes. The cap lifts on the name's first recovery on its own record: a strict new high, or its own ladder lifting a cut.

(R) reserve, structure: the reservation becomes the binding risk limit. The gate now sizes every agent's notional from its mandate's AVAILABLE authority in the DelegationTree (budget − its own spend − what it handed down) × leverage, using a new gate.ts sizeOrder() called after the crowding cuts. The book marks exactly those orders. A new trade audit (tradeViolations → BookInvariantError at "trade") runs every tick between sizing and marking. It checks gross notional ≤ available × leverage, that a revoked or expired agent trades nothing, that no instrument is off the allowlist, and it also flags non-finite values, unknown nodes, and missing or reordered orders. A new onTrade seam hands the sized orders to an outside execution layer or a test before the audit.

loops.title: Every stop-out goes on the operator's record, and the mandate tree is audited against its own log
loops.note: Both structural, no utility claimed: bit-identical on both sealed blocks (every paired change exactly 0). A stop-out now files a 'stop-out' incident (a loss, never misconduct, never a slash) against the agent's operator, and new grants and hires for an operator over its stop-out limit are refused. The book rebuilds the tree from its own event log at every audit, so a write that bypassed the API is caught even when it keeps every invariant. Limits: the log is not signed (a forged event can hide a write), replay holds in memory only (snapshot JSON does not carry the grant and prior-budget fields), and the audit makes the arena about 25% slower. The wildcard researcher returned nothing.

merged.angle: incident (structure): every stop-out now files an incident against the agent's operator, and that record is screened before any new grant or hire for the operator

replay (structure): the mandate tree can be audited from its own event log. DelegationTree.replay(events) rebuilds a tree from the log, verifyAgainstLog() lists every way the live tree differs from that rebuild, and runBook runs the check at the start, trade and end audits of every tick.

loops.title: The audit survives persistence: snapshots replay, and the event log is hash-chained
loops.note: Structural, no utility claimed: bit-identical on both sealed blocks. Snapshot JSON now carries what replay needs, replaySnapshot/verifySnapshot rebuild and check a tree from the JSON alone, and every event links to the one before it by SHA-256, so an edited, deleted, inserted or reordered past event shows. It does not stop someone with API access from appending a forged event. The fund console shows a filtered log (no RESIZE events), so that view drops the hash links rather than carry a chain that cannot verify. Both drawdown researchers returned explicit null results: 17 variants, none beat plain deleveraging, and the center book's excess raw drawdown stays a scale effect (lower at the guardrails' volatility).

merged.angle: persist (STRUCTURE): make the replay audit survive persistence. Snapshot JSON now carries each event's grant, before-budget and a SHA-256 hash-chain link. replaySnapshot/verifySnapshot rebuild and check a DelegationTree from the JSON alone, and verifyAgainstLog/replay check the chain.
